entries.core_idea: The narrator reflects on self-identity through the lens of what they are not, revealing a deep fear of rejection and a struggle with honesty and authenticity, while tracing these feelings back to childhood experiences and the desire to live a genuine life.
entries.evidence_excerpt: I’m not honest, but I try my best to be genuine... I think the main, or perhaps only reason people lie is because they’re afraid... Maybe I’m afraid of being dropped, of people finding out that I’m some sort of failure... Those moments when I returned home with a bad grade and had to then endure hours of being shouted at... I think I like this answer to this prompt. I am not an ostrich.

tag_rationales.self_discovery: The narrator engages in introspection and learning about their own fears and values.
tag_rationales.fear_of_rejection: Fear of social rejection motivates much of the narrator’s inner conflict.
tag_rationales.vulnerability: The openness about fear and dishonesty illustrates a willingness to be emotionally exposed.
tag_rationales.authenticity: The narrator’s desire to live genuinely despite their fears underscores this key motif.

entries.core_idea: The narrator reflects on a personal identity transition marked by the end of a chapter defined by resilience, anger, and coping mechanisms, now replaced by emptiness, coldness, and existential questioning.
entries.evidence_excerpt: I had been closing a chapter in my life. One written by wanting to be myself in a world that seemed perversely interested in finding ways to kick me down... I felt empty, hopelessly weighed down by all these self-made structures that no one could understand. The driving force of anger had burned to nothing, leaving me cold. Why was I here? Who was to blame? I hated it all.

tag_rationales.self_discovery: The narrator is exploring and re-evaluating their self-identity.
tag_rationales.disillusionment: Expressed through loss of purpose and frustration with self-made defenses.
tag_rationales.existential_questioning: Underlying questions about purpose and existence are central to the reflection.

entries.core_idea: The narrator explores relational dynamics through intimate conversation about empathy, sympathy, and vulnerability, reflecting on the difficulties of truly connecting and the desire to alleviate isolation.
entries.evidence_excerpt: We had talked about empathy and sympathy... To understand one person IS to sympathize with them!... I explained that to understand doesn’t mean that you sympathize... Yet we can hate ourselves... Because then no one would have to feel hopelessly isolated.

tag_rationales.vulnerability: Implied by openness required for such intimate conversations.
tag_rationales.communication: The entry focuses on their dialogue and exchange of ideas.

entries.core_idea: The narrator reflects on a persistent, intimate internal dialogue with an existential question that has accompanied them for over a decade, driving deep philosophical inquiry about life’s meaning, purpose, and the value of existence, shaping their worldview and moral understanding over time.
entries.evidence_excerpt: I wonder if there has been a single day in the past decade where you have not taken up at least some corner of my thoughts... One frenchman even said “There is only one really serious philosophical question, and that is suicide.” ... Remember that time when I thought that life was about what you can leave behind?... I really did read too much fantasy back in the day... I had a stage where I thought life was about hope ...

tag_rationales.existential_questioning: The narrator wrestles continuously with the fundamental question of life’s worth and meaning.
tag_rationales.purpose: The narrative explores changing ideas about what makes life meaningful and worth living.
tag_rationales.moral_idealism: Reflection on living according to ideals such as hope, kindness, and helping others informs moral questioning.

entries.core_idea: Individual identity and reality are fundamentally shaped by one’s thoughts and perceptions, meaning each person creates their own internal world that defines their sense of self and how they interpret the external world.
entries.evidence_excerpt: The person is defined by what they think and why they think it. ... As an extension of this thought, it would be fair to think that the idea is the world. The world is defined by what we think regardless of how the world itself is arranged. ... Every mind is a world for the world is in the eyes of the beholder.

tag_rationales.self_discovery: Highlights the process of understanding how one's thoughts define personal identity.
tag_rationales.mind_over_matter: Emphasizes the concept that thought shapes the experience of the world.
tag_rationales.perception: Focuses on the role of individual perception in creating personal realities.

entries.core_idea: The narrator reflects on the profound challenge of truly expressing their unique inner world through language and art, revealing a deep yearning to be genuinely known and to understand others beyond superficial interactions.
entries.evidence_excerpt: 'How limited our means to do this. All language and art can't cover our whole existence. For my thoughts create a world, and your thoughts your world... I want to be known. I do so very want to be seen. I do so very want to see.'

tag_rationales.self_discovery: The narrator examines their own identity and the desire to understand and be understood.
tag_rationales.vulnerability: Expressed by the openness and fear involved in revealing one's inner world.
tag_rationales.authenticity: The longing to be genuinely seen beyond superficial masks.

entries.core_idea: The narrator contemplates the paradoxical nature of identity as an inescapable, infinite loop full of hidden depths and personal veils, expressing both familiarity and fear toward their own complex self.
entries.evidence_excerpt: Identity, the greatest lie of all. How can I see me from outside myself, when trying to get out leads me back to myself. To try and look at yourself is trying to escape the mobius strip by walking along it. Identity is an infinite trap... I know myself better than I know anybody, and the infinite alleys and curtains that branch and veil. I am afraid of the dark paths, that is why I have drawn curtains over them... Yet who but I can call myself by my own highest name? Who else can tread along these winding roads that split and crack and still comfortably call it home?

tag_rationales.self_discovery: The narrator explores multiple veiled and hidden aspects of self, indicating deep and ongoing self-knowledge pursuit.
tag_rationales.existential_questioning: The paradox of escaping oneself and the infinite trap metaphor reflect deep questions about existence and self.
tag_rationales.concealment: Fear of dark paths and drawing curtains over them suggests hiding or masking parts of the self.

entries.core_idea: The narrator uses the metaphor of learning to depict the creative process as a journey of discovery, refinement, and striving for shared understanding through art, emphasizing the aesthetic sensibility and gradual mastery involved.
entries.evidence_excerpt: Imagine a time before art where a person stumbled upon a brick... They decided this moment... started about capturing it... Then about how there seems to be a line of light on the edge of the darkest edges... One day as he is doing this someone will stop him and say ‘that’s not quite how a brick looks’. It is in this moment that the gap has been closed.

tag_rationales.inspiration: The creative impulse to capture and render the brick signifies the spark that drives artistic creation.
tag_rationales.aesthetics: The attention to form, light, and color relates to aesthetic sensibility.
tag_rationales.skill_building: The progression from rudimentary drawing to nuanced shading shows deliberate craft improvement.

entries.core_idea: The essay presents society as an artificial and malleable construction without absolute truths, emphasizing that social morals and systems are human-made and can be changed through conscious understanding.
entries.evidence_excerpt: Society is a construction. By a construction I mean to say that it carries two important qualities: it is artificial, and it is malleable. Society, being artificial, has no hard and fast truths; no absolute values. So all our morals, justice, and freedoms are all just constructs built on abstract nothings. So all of society is malleable, and nothing that is has to be that way. We can change it.

tag_rationales.culture: Captures society as a shared context shaped by humans.
tag_rationales.social_systems: Emphasizes systemic nature of societal constructs.
tag_rationales.malleability: Highlights that society can be changed.

entries.core_idea: The narrative critiques modern societal pathologies such as bureaucratic complexity, loss of solid moralities, and attention marketization, advocating for systemic awareness and meta-understanding to better see and interact with the complex systems shaping our world.
entries.evidence_excerpt: The progress of science and economy has brought us this far ... But now the themes of the day are a loss of solid moralities, near kafkaesque nightmares of bureaucracy, and marketization of our own attention... The problem is that we need to figure out how to see and interact with the systems that make up our world.

tag_rationales.technology: Highlights role of internet and digital systems in societal issues.
tag_rationales.systemic_critique: Central to the critique of bureaucracy and societal dysfunction.
tag_rationales.meta_understanding: Emphasizes meta-game thinking and awareness of systems.

entries.core_idea: The essay argues for the importance of understanding and engaging in society-building as a meta-game, learning the hidden rules, cultural narratives, and strategic moves that shape social structures to meaningfully influence and better the world.
entries.evidence_excerpt: The full meta-game comes in when we go into society building. In the creation of societies there are moves that we can make, the creation of cultural heroes and villains, a central narrative, celebrations... Society and its beliefs have building blocks.

tag_rationales.culture: Reflects myths, narratives, and shared meaning shaping society.
tag_rationales.meta_game: Captures the concept of strategic understanding of society.
tag_rationales.society_building: Emphasizes active engagement in constructing social realities.
